stages.name: Financial markets
stages.title: Financial markets
stages.sub: How financial markets bring savers and borrowers together, and how interest links the two sides.

steps.q: A bank branch takes deposits from people with spare cash and offers loans to people who want to borrow. Is the bank dealing directly in goods like a shop, or in money and financial claims?
steps.hint: Think about what actually changes hands over the counter: tins of beans, or deposits and loans?

steps.q: You put £500 into a savings account instead of keeping it under your mattress. Has the bank given you a way to store and grow money you are not spending right now?
steps.right: Yes, a way to hold and grow spare money
steps.wrong: No, the bank only moves money about for spenders
steps.hint: What did opening the account let you do with money you were not using today?

steps.q: A small bakery wants £10,000 to buy a new oven but does not have the cash. Can a bank take money that others have deposited and pass it to the bakery as a loan?
steps.right: Yes, deposited money can be lent out to the bakery
steps.wrong: No, deposits must stay untouched until savers withdraw them
steps.hint: Where does a bank get the funds it hands out as loans?

steps.q: If savings accounts paid 0% interest, would many people still bother locking their money away instead of spending it?
steps.wrong: Just as many people would still save
steps.hint: What reward do savers currently get for giving up spending now?
steps.pre: So savers need a reward to hold back cash: that reward is interest paid on savings.
